title: Action Stream Declarative Contracts and SDK Observability (scrapbook)
content:
Purpose

This doc is a working scrapbook for a focused PRD slice: define a small, pragmatic "declarative action stream" contract that the Hosted API can emit and that SDKs will adopt as a first-class surface. The goal is to reduce client-side glue for tool-calling flows, improve observability for production incidents, and enable graceful degradation for partial/streamed structured output.

Why this now

- Customers building tool orchestration want less brittle parsing logic (JSON-in-text) and fewer heuristics when partial responses arrive.
- Current streaming output uses ad-hoc frames + freeform text; SDKs add best-effort parsers that diverge across languages.
- Observable tool calls (start/finish/resolve/fallback) are critical for debugging high-throughput apps (mobile + server).

Problem statement (concise)

Host API streaming currently exposes token streams and "events" (proto-ish). There is no small, battery-included structured frame that expresses:
  - actionable tool invocation intent (tool id, args, call_id)
  - partial structured payloads (incremental JSON fragments)
  - confidence/degradation hints + provenance
  - lifecycle telemetry hooks (attempt, retry, fallback)

Consequences: inconsistent client parsing, tool reconciliation bugs, poor production observability and longer MTTR for failures.

Goals (measurable)

1) Reduce client parsing error rate for tool-calling demos by 80% in our internal SDKs (measured by test harness).
2) Provide a minimum viable streaming contract that allows a mobile SDK to render intermediate actionable UI (progress, partial args) without custom parsers.
3) Emit standardized telemetry for each action frame so SRE/product can alert on malformed tool calls, repeated fallbacks, and cold-start/latency anomalies.

Non-goals

- Not designing the entire typed-schema system for every domain. This is a pragmatic incremental contract for actions and partial structured payloads.
- Not locking customers into strict schema validation server-side; we provide opt-in strictness.

Proposed surface (high level)

- Streaming frames will include a new top-level frame type: ACTION_FRAME. ACTION_FRAME is a compact newline-delimited JSON object (single-line) emitted interleaved with regular token streaming. SDKs will detect lines starting with "[action]" prefix to locate frames reliably across transports.

- ACTION_FRAME schema (flat-ish initial fields):
    - frame_type: "action"
    - call_id: string (idempotency/trace link)
    - tool: string (registered tool identifier)
    - stage: one of ["intent", "args_partial", "args_complete", "invoke", "result_partial", "result_complete", "fallback"]
    - payload: base64-encoded chunk OR compact JSON string (explained below)
    - provenance: optional string (model_version / variant)
    - confidence_hint: optional numeric string (0-1)
    - suggested_fallback: optional string

Note: fields are strings to keep the wire format tolerant across tokenizers; SDKs will parse and cast.

Why newline-delimited single-line JSON + prefix?

- Resilient to streaming transports and to client raw token consumption.
- Easy to spot in logs and tracing pipes (grep friendly).
- Minimizes protocol changes while supporting incremental payloads.

Examples (conceptual)

1) early intent frame (UI can surface suggested action)
[action]{"frame_type":"action","call_id":"c-8a3","tool":"calendar.create_event","stage":"intent","payload":"{"summary":"Plan Q1 sync"}","provenance":"rw-1.2"}

2) partial args frame (two fragments emitted as streaming continues)
[action]{"frame_type":"action","call_id":"c-8a3","tool":"calendar.create_event","stage":"args_partial","payload":"{"start":"2025-02-10T10:00:00Z"}"}
[action]{"frame_type":"action","call_id":"c-8a3","tool":"calendar.create_event","stage":"args_complete","payload":"{"end":"2025-02-10T10:30:00Z","attendees":["e@example.com"]}"}

3) invoke + result_partial frames (server signals call and streamed result)
[action]{"frame_type":"action","call_id":"c-8a3","tool":"calendar.create_event","stage":"invoke","payload":""}
[action]{"frame_type":"action","call_id":"c-8a3","tool":"calendar.create_event","stage":"result_partial","payload":"{"event_id":"evt_12f"}"}
[action]{"frame_type":"action","call_id":"c-8a3","tool":"calendar.create_event","stage":"result_complete","payload":"{"url":"https://cal/evt_12f"}"}

SDK ergonomics (developer-facing)

- auto-detect frames: SDK runtime exposes a small helper that splits token stream by newline and returns parsed ACTION_FRAMEs in a typed callback (onActionFrame).
- optimistic client UI primitives: onActionFrame(intent) -> render suggested action chip; onActionFrame(args_partial) -> render placeholder inputs progressively; onActionFrame(invoke) -> disable edits and show spinner; onActionFrame(result_partial/complete) -> show result and enable snapshotting.
- idempotency/ack: SDK will surface call_id to app; app can pass a client-generated id to pin a tool invocation and deduplicate retries.
- fallback handling: SDK exposes a simple policy interface (auto-accept fallback, prompt user, or send to server for policy).

Observability & telemetry (production)

Emit standardized events behind the scenes (these are small records that appear in the Console and in Trace spans):
  - action.frame.emitted  (metadata: call_id, stage, tool, provenance, size_bytes)
  - action.invoke.latency (call_id, tool, start_ts, end_ts, region, success:boolean)
  - action.fallback.trigger (call_id, reason, suggested_fallback)
  - action.parse.error (sdk_lang, error_kind, raw_frame_sample)

Design notes:
- We keep telemetry minimal but actionable: correlate by call_id to link frames to traces and downstream tool requests.
- Allow customers to enable PII-scrubbing for frame.payload before it leaves the host if they choose.

Backward compatibility strategy

- Default behavior: existing clients ignore unknown bracketed lines. We avoid breaking by using a unique prefix "[action]" so older SDKs treat it as text.
- Opt-in stricter mode: tenant-level flag that enforces schema validation and surfaces server-side errors when frames violate expected shape. Useful for enterprise customers.

Operational concerns / costs

- Some customers will emit large payloads in frames (attachments). We will introduce a per-frame size cap (e.g., 32KB) and provide a streaming attachment handle pattern (emit a small ref, then upload via multipart).
- Telemetry volume: action.frame.emitted is high-cardinality; we will sample frames at 1% by default, 100% for enterprise monitoring.

Migration + rollout plan (phases)

Phase 0 (internal experiment, 2 sprints): implement frame emitter for a small LLM route, wire internal SDK helper, and run a developer lab with 3 integrators.
Phase 1 (beta, 4 sprints): support opt-in tenant flag, surface telemetry in Console (basic charts + trace linking), SDK bindings for JS + Python.
Phase 2 (GA, 6 sprints): introduce size caps, attachment ref pattern, mobile SDK adapters, and SDK helper for UI primitives.

Risk register (quick)

- Risk: customers exhaust tokens by embedding heavy payloads in frames. Mitigation: enforce size caps and warn in Console usage.
- Risk: model hallucination produces malformed JSON payloads mid-stream. Mitigation: SDK tolerant parsing, server-side best-effort repair attempts, parse.error telemetry to trigger auto-regressions.
- Risk: fragmentation across SDKs (JS, Py, Go). Mitigation: single canonical parser in rust that we compile to wasm/bindings for other SDKs. (proto-idea)

Open questions (todo)

- Should payload be base64 for binary-safe transport, or compact JSON string (smaller but requires quoting)? tradeoffs in tokenization and readability.
- What is the right default sampling rate for telemetry to balance observability vs cost?
- Do we want a small typed registry for tools (tool_name -> schema) stored in customer's workspace to enable client-side validation?

Implementation notes for eng

- Streaming emitter sits in model response post-processor; should be low-latency and idempotent so retries don't duplicate frames.
- Add a lightweight deterministic frame id (call_id) assigned during planning stage in the model-driver so SDKs and Console share the same id immediately.
- Create a devkit repo example: hosted-api/action-frames-playground with a small JS SPA demo that shows incremental UI updates.

Next steps (owner: Priya)

- Sync with Applied ML on hallucination heuristics (Evan) — due 2025-01-20.
- Create a small PoC in SDK-js to detect frames and surface onActionFrame callbacks (Marcus) — due 2025-01-28.
- Draft Console telemetry panel mock (Lena) — due 2025-02-05.

Notes to self / brainstorming fragments

- Could use an alternate prefix style: "<<ACTION>>" for UTF-safety in some mobile pipes. Need to test.
- Consider a compact binary frame in the long term (proto over websocket) for heavy-duty customers.
- Example UX: Gmail-esque suggested actions that fill a draft with partial args as the model streams. Delight factor could drive adoption.

References and logs

- Slack thread: #prod-hosted-api (see message ts 1702002341)
- Internal integration notes: GH PR 321 shows prototype parser.
- Customers asking for this: demo call with Acme AI on 2024-11-12 (notes in CS folder).

-- end of scrapbook --
